newsitem.title: UK: Esso sees fierce German petrol market to 1998.
newsitem.headline: Esso sees fierce German petrol market to 1998.

text.p: A fiercely competitive retail petrol market in Germany, rivalling the price war in the U.K., will continue into next year and keep margins at the bare bones, Esso Petroleum said on Thursday.

Daily changes in pump prices are occurring at a swifter pace due to a stagnant wholesale gasoline market and a mushrooming of petrol stations, Karl Schult-Bornemann, Hamburg-based spokesman for Esso, a unit of U.S. oil giant Exxon Corp, told Reuters.
Germany is an echo of Britian where Esso launched its Pricewatch campaign in early 1996, promising to match its lowest-priced competitors in order to hang on to its market share.
"There is a price-watch movement among petrol stations going on all the time," the spokesman said. "This has happened for 20 years so it's nothing new."

"The only thing new in the last two years is the speed in which the price goes down has increased," he added. "It's pretty clear that the strong and fierce competition will go on for more than six or nine months."
Esso's 1,500 German stations change their pump prices about 2,000 times a week, more than once a day, he said.
German stations total 18,000, with the five major oil companies grabbing 60 percent of that, he said.

East German stations have grown from 1,200 in 1990 to roughly 2,000 to 2,500, he said. Because investments in the stations have already been made, there will be no quick end to the price competition, he explained.
"It is at least one of the most competitive in Europe and it might be that the competition in the U.K. is equalling what we have here, but I can't really judge," he said.

Esso had no comment on the decision of some German stations selling its brand to consider filing a complaint with the European Commission on the grounds that regulations of vertical restraint were being violated.
German Esso retailers are planning to meet with U.K. and Dutch counterparts in Brussels on June 11.
